cases.rendered:
Under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a small business is a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Under that definition, any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Gross turnover means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover"]

In determining whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company for VAT returns, the value of the supply of a capital asset of the person is excluded. The value of a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business is also excluded. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- No Act called the Nigeria Small Business Tax Act 2025 is among the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover" (gazette pages A 504, A 505)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10) (gazette page A 277)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-references: subsection (4), sections 105 and 107 (cited) against subsection (5), sections 100 and 102 (National Assembly). (DR-198)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-reference: section 152 of the Nigeria Tax Act (cited) against section 151 (National Assembly text, the same section under its numbering, DR-000). (DR-199)

cases.question: What do sections 22 and 290 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act say about VAT returns?

claims.text: A taxable person must, for value added tax, with or without a notice, and whether or not an economic activity has taken place, submit a return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month.
Where the Service grants an extension of the period for filing returns under section 22, the extension does not imply an extension of time to pay the tax.
The returns must contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and value added tax payable in respect of all taxable supplies in the preceding month.
The filing rule in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business.

A small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption granted to small businesses under this Part, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns.
The opt-out choice in section 22(5) does not apply to companies engaged in petroleum operations as defined in the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025.
A business, upon ceasing to be a small business, shall file monthly VAT returns.

In determining whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company, the value of the supply of a capital asset of the person is excluded, as is the value of a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business.
A taxable person granted the exemption in subsection (4) is exempt from sections 105 and 107 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act and section 152 of the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025.
Where technology is deployed by the Service, a taxable person shall render returns in real time or at such other time as the Service may prescribe.
For the purpose of attribution, any return under section 22 shall provide details of consumption of taxable supplies, irrespective of where the return is filed.

cases.rendered:
Every taxable person shall register with the relevant tax authority and obtain a Tax ID for the purpose of compliance with tax obligations. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 4]

Every ministry, department or agency of the Federal or a State government, and every Local Government shall register for tax and obtain a Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 5]

A non-resident person that supplies taxable goods or services to any person in Nigeria, or derives income from Nigeria, shall register for tax purposes and obtain a Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 6]

A non-resident person who derives only passive income from investment in Nigeria may not be required to register for tax, but shall provide relevant information as may be prescribed by the Service. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 6]

The relevant tax authority may issue guidelines for the purpose of giving effect to the section on non-resident persons. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 6]

"Registration" means the action or process of registering or of being registered for tax purposes in accordance with the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "registration"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether the asker is a taxable person, a government body or a non-resident person, so they do not settle whether the asker needs to register.
- The definition of "taxable person" is not among the passages.
- Any guidelines issued by the relevant tax authority under section 6 are not among the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 4 (gazette page A 266)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 5 (gazette page A 266)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 6 (gazette pages A 266, A 267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "registration" (gazette page A 331)

claims.text: A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs.

Separately, where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, a sum equal to 10% of the amount of tax payable is added to it, subject to section 67 of the Act.

Where tax is not paid within the prescribed period, the tax due also carries interest from the date it becomes payable until it is paid. For naira remittances the rate is the prevailing monetary policy rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria plus a spread determined by the Minister. For foreign currency remittances it is the prevailing SOFR or any successor rate, plus 10% or such other spread as the Minister determines.

cases.rendered:
A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101]

The same provision adds an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101]

Separately, where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, a sum equal to 10% of the amount of tax payable is added to it, subject to section 67 of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

Where tax is not paid within the prescribed period, the tax due also carries interest from the date it becomes payable until it is paid. For naira remittances the rate is the prevailing monetary policy rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria plus a spread determined by the Minister. For foreign currency remittances it is the prevailing SOFR or any successor rate, plus 10% or such other spread as the Minister determines. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The interest under section 65(1)(b) and (c) is compound interest and applies to all tax debts that remain unpaid as at the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether the late-filing penalty applies to a VAT return specifically, or which provisions set VAT filing deadlines.
- The total in naira needs a calculation of the number of months of failure and the amount of any unpaid tax, which the passages do not do.
- The question does not say whether any tax was left unpaid, so the 10% addition and interest may not apply.
- Section 67, which section 65 refers to, is not among the passages.
- The Minister's spread over the monetary policy rate is not among the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101 (gazette page A 312)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65 (gazette pages A 298, A 299)

- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Interest is SOFR plus 10% or such other spread as the authority determines in the cited text; the National Assembly text says SOFR plus a spread to be determined, without the 10%. (DR-243)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Only the cited text makes the interest in subsection (1)(b) and (c) compound and applies it to tax debts unpaid at commencement. (DR-245)

<question>

<gaps>

cases.rendered:
Where a company's effective tax rate in a year of assessment is less than 15%, the company must recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

This rule applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

"Effective tax rate" means the aggregate covered tax paid by a company for a year of assessment divided by the profits of the company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

For this section, "profits" means the net profits before tax as reported in the audited financial statement less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost for the year. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

"Multinational group" means MNE group. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "multinational group"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The top-up amount needs a calculation (the profits figure under section 57, the covered tax paid, and the gap to 15%), which is not done here.
- The question gives profits of ₦2 billion, but the section defines profits as audited net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. The depreciation and personnel cost figures are not given.
- The passages do not say whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group, or whether the group is the kind of group the section covers.
- The passages do not define "covered tax" or "MNE group", so they do not show how the 9% rate was reached or whether it counts as the effective tax rate under section 57.
- Subsection (3) of section 57 is not among the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "multinational group" (gazette page A 506)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.question: Our company gave money to a church school's building fund. Can we deduct that donation, and is there a limit?

claims.text: For working out a company's profits or loss from any source chargeable with tax under Chapter Two, the amount of any donation the company makes for that period to a fund, body or institution in Nigeria to which section 164 applies shall be deducted. This is subject to the section's provisions.
Section 164 applies to donations made to religious, charitable, educational and scientific institutions, established in Nigeria.
A donation may be deducted from the profits of that period even if it is of a revenue or capital nature.
A company making a deduction for a donation shall provide the requisite document evidencing the donation to the relevant tax authority.
The total deduction allowed to a company under this section for any year of assessment shall not exceed an amount equal to 10% of the company's profit before tax for that year.
For a donation other than in cash, the value for this section is the lower of the market value at the time of the donation or the consideration paid for the item when it was acquired.

gaps: The passages do not say whether a church school, or its building fund, counts as a religious or educational institution established in Nigeria, or whether the fund is a body to which section 164 applies.
The passages do not say whether a gift to a building fund is treated as a donation to the institution itself.
The 10% limit on the profit before tax figure is a calculation that is not done here.

For working out a company's profits or loss from any source chargeable with tax under Chapter Two, the amount of any donation the company makes for that period to a fund, body or institution in Nigeria to which section 164 applies shall be deducted. This is subject to the section's provisions. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

Section 164 applies to donations made to religious, charitable, educational and scientific institutions, established in Nigeria. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

A donation may be deducted from the profits of that period even if it is of a revenue or capital nature. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

A company making a deduction for a donation shall provide the requisite document evidencing the donation to the relevant tax authority. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

The total deduction allowed to a company under this section for any year of assessment shall not exceed an amount equal to 10% of the company's profit before tax for that year. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

For a donation other than in cash, the value for this section is the lower of the market value at the time of the donation or the consideration paid for the item when it was acquired. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s72 subsections (2) to (4): banks and government bodies demand a certificate for the three years before the current year of assessment for the listed transactions.
cases.question: Why would my bank ask for a tax clearance certificate, and how many years must it cover?

claims.text: Any commercial bank with which a person has any dealing in respect of the transactions listed in subsection (4) shall demand from that person a tax clearance certificate of three years immediately preceding the current year of assessment.

The listed transactions are: application for certificate of occupancy, approval of building plans, application for award of contract by government or its agencies, application for firearms licence, application for import and export licence, and application for trade licence.

A tax clearance certificate shall disclose, for the last three years of assessment, total profits or chargeable income, tax payable, tax paid, and tax outstanding or alternatively a statement that no tax is due.

The relevant tax authority shall issue a certificate within two weeks of the person's demand where it is of the opinion that tax assessed has been fully paid or that no tax is due, or else give reasons for the denial.

gaps: The passages do not say which specific dealing a given bank has with the person in the question, so they do not show which listed transaction, if any, applies to that bank's request.

claims.text: Every taxable person shall register with the relevant tax authority and obtain a Tax ID for the purpose of compliance with tax obligations.

A relevant tax authority may, based on the information available to it, register and issue a Tax ID to a person who should apply for one but failed to do so.
The relevant tax authority shall promptly notify a person registered and issued with a Tax ID in this way of the registration and Tax ID.
A Tax ID is a condition for entering into a contract with any federal or state ministry, department or agency and local government.
A statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered person is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦5,000,000.

cases.rendered:
Every taxable person shall register with the relevant tax authority and obtain a Tax ID for the purpose of compliance with tax obligations. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 4]

A taxable person who fails or refuses to register for tax under section 4 is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs and ₦25,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

A relevant tax authority may, based on the information available to it, register and issue a Tax ID to a person who should apply for one but failed to do so. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 7]

The relevant tax authority shall promptly notify a person registered and issued with a Tax ID in this way of the registration and Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 7]

A Tax ID is a condition for entering into a contract with any federal or state ministry, department or agency and local government. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8]

A statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered person is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦5,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The total penalty over a given number of months needs a calculation, which is not done here.
- The passages do not say whether the company counts as a taxable person; that link is not stated in them.
- The passages do not say how or when the penalty is assessed or collected.

cases.rendered:
Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company, and for a small company the rate is 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A business providing professional services is not classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Any other company (one that is not a small company) is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)

cases.question: We bought ₦9 million of office furniture. How much capital allowance can we claim each year?

claims.text: Capital expenditure on furniture and fittings, including those used in vessels, ships, aircrafts, trains, plants, and buildings for the purposes of trade or business, is qualifying capital expenditure (qualifying furniture and fittings expenditure).
Furniture and Fittings Expenditure is in Class 2, which has a rate of 20% in Table I.

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance at the rate in Table I is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business.

A proviso says 1% of qualifying capital expenditure is recorded in the capital allowance computation schedule for statistical purposes until the asset is disposed of. It is a notional amount and does not increase or reduce the capital allowance claimable.
Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.
The allowance is made for a year if, at the end of the basis period, the person owns the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
The residue of qualifying expenditure at a date is the total qualifying expenditure incurred on or before that date for the asset, less the total capital allowance made for it before that date.

An allowance shall not be made for a year of assessment unless it is claimed for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.
Where an allowance is not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business, it shall be carried forward to a subsequent period.

The allowance is subtracted from the remainder of the assessable profits or income for the year. If there is no remainder or an insufficient remainder, the deduction or the part not yet made is treated as a deduction for the next year and succeeding years until fully utilised.

Where the owner partly uses an asset for a trade or business, the allowance is apportioned to the trade or business as may be reasonable. The relevant tax authority makes necessary adjustments if it considers the basis of apportionment not just and reasonable.

cases.question: Our input VAT this month is ₦1.8 million and our output VAT is ₦2.5 million. How much do we pay?

claims.text: Where output VAT exceeds input VAT, a taxable person must remit the excess to the Service not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025.
VAT a taxable person pays to a supplier on a taxable supply made to it is called input VAT.
VAT a taxable person collects on making taxable supplies is called output VAT.
A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month.
The VAT return must contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and VAT payable on all taxable supplies in the preceding month.
If the Service grants an extension of the period for filing the return, this does not extend the time to pay the tax.

Input tax incurred on a taxable supply may be deducted from the tax payable on taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies.
Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted.
The subsection (1) filing rule does not apply to a small business.

gaps: The amount payable needs a subtraction of input VAT from output VAT, which is a calculation not done here.
Whether the whole input VAT qualifies for deduction is not stated, such as how much relates to taxable supplies.
Whether the business is a small business is not stated.

Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A business providing professional services is not classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Separately, a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, or any other company with aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment, must recompute and pay additional tax if its effective tax rate is less than 15%, so that its effective tax rate equals 15%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether furniture sales count as a business providing professional services is not stated in the passages.
- Whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group is not stated in the question.
- Whether the turnover and fixed asset figures meet the small company test on the passages' terms is a comparison the passages leave to be done; no calculation is made here.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s73(1)-(4): advance rulings on application by a taxable person, issued within 21 days or with written reasons.
cases.question: Can my company ask the tax service for a written ruling on how a law applies before we go ahead with a deal?

claims.text: An advance ruling may be issued to give clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, as long as the ruling does not amend or replace the law.

The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling on an application by a taxable person within 21 days of receiving the application, or give reasons in writing for being unable to issue the ruling.
An application is to be made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to a tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more parties to it.

The definition of advance ruling includes a written opinion or decision given to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction, a proposed transaction or any tax matter, to give direction or clarification.
An application must contain the taxpayer's details, a complete description of the issue or transaction and its financial implications, if any, and a description of the impact on tax liability.

An application must also contain details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions on the issue, the legal basis relied on, the reasons the ruling should be granted, and a written statement on whether the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction.

The relevant tax authority may request additional information from an applicant, and where necessary shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations or provide clarifications.
An applicant may withdraw an application at any time before a ruling is issued.

The relevant tax authority may reject an application where it requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on the laws of a foreign country, an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the interpretation of the Constitution, an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious, or a ruling that will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or connected persons.
A ruling is limited to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given, is rendered on the set of facts before the relevant tax authority, and cannot be of general application.

An advance ruling is void where the transaction described is materially different from the one actually carried out, where there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or where an assumption made or condition imposed by the relevant tax authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer.

An advance ruling ceases to be effective where the tax law provision it concerned is repealed or amended in a way that materially affects it, or where a court overturns or modifies the interpretation of the tax law on which it is based.

A company is a company as defined under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, or a corporate body formed under any other written law, and includes any association, whether incorporated in or outside Nigeria.

gaps: The passages do not say which body is the relevant tax authority for a particular tax.
The prescribed form and manner for an application are not set out in the passages.
Whether the company is a taxable person or a party to the particular deal depends on facts not given in the question.

An advance ruling may be issued to give clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, as long as the ruling does not amend or replace the law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 73(1) to (4)]

The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling on an application by a taxable person within 21 days of receiving the application, or give reasons in writing for being unable to issue the ruling. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 73(1) to (4)]

An application is to be made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to a tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more parties to it. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 73(1) to (4)]

The definition of advance ruling includes a written opinion or decision given to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction, a proposed transaction or any tax matter, to give direction or clarification. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "advance ruling"]

An application must contain the taxpayer's details, a complete description of the issue or transaction and its financial implications, if any, and a description of the impact on tax liability. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 73(5) to (8)]

An application must also contain details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions on the issue, the legal basis relied on, the reasons the ruling should be granted, and a written statement on whether the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 73(5) to (8)]

The relevant tax authority may request additional information from an applicant, and where necessary shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations or provide clarifications. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 73(5) to (8)]

An applicant may withdraw an application at any time before a ruling is issued. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 73(5) to (8)]

The relevant tax authority may reject an application where it requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on the laws of a foreign country, an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the interpretation of the Constitution, an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious, or a ruling that will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or connected persons. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 74]

A ruling is limited to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given, is rendered on the set of facts before the relevant tax authority, and cannot be of general application. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 75]

An advance ruling is void where the transaction described is materially different from the one actually carried out, where there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or where an assumption made or condition imposed by the relevant tax authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 75]

An advance ruling ceases to be effective where the tax law provision it concerned is repealed or amended in a way that materially affects it, or where a court overturns or modifies the interpretation of the tax law on which it is based. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 75]

A company is a company as defined under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, or a corporate body formed under any other written law, and includes any association, whether incorporated in or outside Nigeria. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "company"]

Where a Nigerian company declares dividend out of profits on which no tax is payable because there are no total profits, or because total profits are less than the dividend declared, the company paying the dividend is charged to tax at the rate prescribed in section 56 of the Act. This rule does not apply to franked investment income as provided in the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 9]

This rule does not apply to distributions by a real estate investment company to its shareholders from rental income and dividend income received on behalf of those shareholders, whether paid out of profits of the year of declaration or of previous reporting periods. claims.text: VAT that a taxable person pays to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person is called input VAT.
VAT that a taxable person collects on making taxable supplies is called output VAT.

Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, the taxable person is entitled to use the excess tax as a credit against subsequent months. This applies by the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025.
A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not used as a credit, on request to the Service and on providing the information or documents the Service may require.

Input tax on a taxable supply to a registered person may be deducted from the tax payable on its taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent that it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies.
Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted.
Input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred.
The input tax that may be deducted is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of the Act.

<question>
This month the VAT I paid on purchases is more than the VAT I collected on sales. What happens to the extra?
</question>

cases.rendered:
VAT that a taxable person pays to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person is called input VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152]

VAT that a taxable person collects on making taxable supplies is called output VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154]

Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, the taxable person is entitled to use the excess tax as a credit against subsequent months. This applies by the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not used as a credit, on request to the Service and on providing the information or documents the Service may require. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Input tax on a taxable supply to a registered person may be deducted from the tax payable on its taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent that it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

The input tax that may be deducted is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether the purchases in question were made for taxable supplies, or whether the person is a taxable or registered person.
- The passages do not give the due date of the relevant tax return under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025.
- Any calculation of the actual excess amount is not covered.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152 (gazette page A 473)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154 (gazette page A 474)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156 (gazette pages A 474, A 475)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154: Cross-reference: the rate is in section 148 (gazette); the National Assembly text cites section 146, which is not its rate section (147). (DR-061)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156: The gazette lets a person whose supplies are zero-rated pay VAT on its inputs and then claim a refund; the National Assembly text has no such subsection. (DR-067)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156: Because of the gazette's extra subsection (4), gazette (5) and (6) are National Assembly (4) and (5). (DR-068)

claims.text: A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria shall register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies.

Where a non-resident person is making taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person to whom the supply is made in Nigeria shall withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service.
The Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier of taxable supplies, to collect the VAT and remit it to the Service.

Where a person appointed by the Service has made a taxable supply to a taxable person in Nigeria, the taxable person shall not have the obligation to withhold the VAT, except where the person appointed has failed to collect the VAT.
A non-resident person that makes a taxable supply to a person in Nigeria may appoint a representative for the purpose of compliance with its VAT obligations.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom taxable supplies are made in Nigeria and who was issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 shall be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction or as may be prescribed by the Service.

The remission must be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.

cases.question: My company made ₦120 million profit this year. How much company income tax will it pay?

claims.text: Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%.
Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.

The total profits of a company are its total assessable profits from all sources, including chargeable gains, less any loss ascertained in accordance with subsection (6) and capital allowance under Part I of the First Schedule.

Where the effective tax rate of a company in a year of assessment is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. This applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment.

Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

The total profits of a company are its total assessable profits from all sources, including chargeable gains, less any loss ascertained in accordance with subsection (6) and capital allowance under Part I of the First Schedule. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4)]

Where the effective tax rate of a company in a year of assessment is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. This applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether the company is a small company, so it is not clear whether 0% or 30 per cent applies.
- The passages as supplied do not define a small company.
- The question gives profit but not total profits after losses and capital allowances, so the taxable amount cannot be worked out from the passages.
- The company's turnover and whether it belongs to an MNE group are not stated, so it is not clear whether the 15% effective tax rate rule applies.
- Subsection (6) of section 27, which section 27(1) refers to, is not among the passages.
- The tax calculation itself is not done here.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4) (gazette pages A 412, A 413)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4): The National Assembly text requires companies in the priority sector to obtain a certificate of acceptance from the Industrial Inspectorate Department for qualifying capital expenditure; the gazette has no such condition. (DR-039)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)
